title: Oscar Klein and Muriel, Billie Holiday silhouette idea
summary: He describes his idea for Muriel to sing as Billie behind a shim.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: I was in Zürich Sunday. They're building a new hotel in Zürich. You know the Park? That's where Oscar Klein and Muriel live. Did you know them?
Yeah, I know them. Yeah. He's a nice trumpet player.
Yeah. I saw them Saturday night.

Like Billie? Yeah. You know what? I wanted to bring Muriel to America and design a Billie Holiday shim silhouette and let Muriel sing behind that shim and do a whole concert. You'd see the band but you just wouldn't see her. And for the finale, she would come out from behind the shim and sing...da-da-da da-da-da da-da_da da-da-da DAH..."

And sing "Gloomy Sunday." With the lights down so you'd just see the figure but you can't see who she is. when..da-da-da da-da-da da-da-da DAH-ah Gloomy Sunday." And the lights would come up. And I think that would be a bitch.

Why? Because she sings so much like Billie until people get mad, you know. They resent it. (Laughter). You know? I told Barney. I said, "I don't want to hear no god-damn white woman sing like Billie." I said, "But, this is something." You know they get insulted, you know. They... you hurt their feelings, you know?

But let her do the whole concert behind the shim, you know, and Billie Holiday's silhouette, with the trumpet player playing, and then, let her come out, and them lights so dim you can't see her, and when she say, "Gloomy SUN...day," then the lights come on bright.
